newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin, Clinton to meet in March, Kremlin says.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin, Clinton to meet in March, Kremlin says.

text.p: Presidents Boris Yeltsin of Russia and Bill Clinton of the United States spoke by telephone on Thursday and agreed to meet next March, a Kremlin spokesman said.
The summit will probably take place in the United States, chief presidential spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky told Interfax news agency. A Kremlin press officer confirmed the report.
Itar-Tass news agency later quoted a presidential spokesman saying the venue was likely to be Washington.
The two leaders, who last met in Moscow in April during an international summit on nuclear safety, both expressed their satisfaction with efforts to develop relations, Interfax said.
The Kremlin did not say how long the conversation lasted.
Yeltsin, 65, was spending his first day at a country home near Moscow, exactly a month after a heart bypass operation.

Clinton, who has been having problems with hoarseness, was told by doctors on Wednesday, to rest his voice for three or four days. The White House has admitted the president was having trouble keeping quiet.

The Kremlin had said on Tuesday that Yeltsin would meet Clinton in the first half of 1997. The two leaders had agreed on the meeting after U.S. Vice President Al Gore and Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin met in Lisbon on Monday.
